title: The Chalk Line
moral: Justice means being fair even when we must give up some space, comfort, or advantage for others.

pages.text:
The children in Building C had drawn a chalk line across the courtyard.

"This side is for cricket," said Armaan.

"That side is for skipping," said Jia.

For two days, the plan worked well.

Then on Wednesday, the cricket ball kept rolling across the line. The skipping rope kept swinging into the cricket side.

Soon everyone was arguing.

"Your ball came here!"

"Your rope hit me!"

"Your chalk line is crooked!"

Armaan looked down. It was crooked. But he said, "It is artistic."

Jia crossed her arms. "It is unfair."

The younger children sat on the steps, waiting. They had brought a small plastic bat and a skipping rope with pink handles, but no one was letting them play.

Armaan wanted the cricket side to stay bigger. Jia wanted more space for skipping.

Then little Mehul stood up.

"Can we play too?" he asked.

No one answered.

His sister held the pink rope quietly.

Armaan suddenly remembered when he was younger. The older boys never gave him a turn. He used to stand near the wall, pretending he did not care.

But he had cared a lot.

He picked up the chalk.

"What are you doing?" Jia asked.

"Drawing a better line," Armaan said.

This time, he made three spaces.

One for cricket.

One for skipping.

One small middle space for younger children to play anything they wanted.

Jia looked at it.

"Our space is smaller," she said.

"So is ours," Armaan said. "But now everyone gets some."

The first few minutes were messy. A ball rolled into the middle. A rope landed near the wickets. Mehul ran in circles for no clear reason.

Jia laughed. "What game is he playing?"

Mehul shouted, "Fast walking!"

Soon, everyone adjusted.

The courtyard became noisy again, but this time it was happy noise.

At sunset, the chalk line had become faint under many feet.

Armaan looked at it and smiled.

A fair line is not always the line that gives us the most. Sometimes it is the line that leaves space for everyone.
